data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims the Decoy Perturbation is the ONLY single-evaluation evidence distinguishing reliability from compliance, but this is false: cross-validation of reasoning traces offers a second, distinct single-evaluation signal. When a non-expert panel arrives at the objectively correct answer, one can examine whether each member's checklist annotations contain task-relevant justifications that coherently map to the verified outcome versus mere item-by-item 'pass' markings with no mechanistic linkage to the answer. A genuinely reliable panel produces calibrated reasoning artifacts (e.g., flagging specific evidence for each check, noting uncertainty); a merely compliant panel produces uniform, content-free affirmations. This reasoning-trace audit occurs within the same single evaluation and does not require inserting a logically irrelevant or contradictory requirement, yet it still separates reliability from compliance.
